## Slug
`research/backward/bipartite-threshold-shadow.md` — "Superlogarithmic lower bound via the bipartition's threshold shadow."

## What the skeleton says
The goal `f(n) = ω(log n)` is reduced through the cube's bipartition (`E` = even weight, `O` = odd weight, every edge crosses). Writing `A = S∩E`, `B = S∩O` with `a+b = 2^{n-1}+1`, the condition `D(S) ≤ d` forces `B ⊆ O_{≤d}(A)`, where `O_{≤d}(A) = {x ∈ O : |N(x)∩A| ≤ d}` is a **threshold shadow** — a quantity that is a *maximum by construction*, exactly the shape the problem statement says the lower bound must come from. The chain is one-sided on purpose: it suffices to show `|O_{≤d₀(n)}(A)| ≤ 2^{n-1} − |A|` for **all** `A ⊆ E`, which forces `f(n) ≥ d₀(n)+1`. No averaging anywhere.

## Gaps left open (3, all `status: open`)
- **`G-bip-reduce`** — the bijection and the contrapositive reduction (trivial, dischargeable today by a Lean formalisation + a brute-force cross-check of `D(S)` against `f_exact(n)` for `n ≤ 4`).
- **`G-threshold-shadow`** — the extremal statement that `|O_{≤d}(A)|` is maximised (at fixed `|A|`) by a Hamming ball / initial segment. `next`: ILP argmax hunt for `n ≤ 6`, plus a compression/shifting proof attempt.
- **`G-threshold-analysis`** — that the resulting upper bound `U_d(a)` satisfies `U_d(a) ≤ 2^{n-1} − a` at a superlogarithmic `d₀(n)`. `next`: symbolic closed form for the ball value, solve for the critical `d*(n)`; if `d*(n) = Θ(log n)` the obstruction is located *exactly*.

No lemma was discharged because `research/CLAIMS.md` is empty — there is nothing in the run yet to check a lemma against.

The "thirty-year gap" between log n and sqrt(n) in this problem is CLOSED by Hao Huang's spectral argument (2019), and this run has re-derived and mechanically verified it. Verified exactly: (1) signed adjacency A_1=[[0,1],[1,0]], A_n=[[A_{n-1},I],[I,-A_{n-1}]] satisfies A_n²=n·I exactly for n=1..8 (sympy Integer), support exactly the cube's edges, spectrum ±√n each mult 2^{n-1} for n=2..10. (2) For EVERY admissible S (|S|=2^{n-1}+1), λ_max(A_n[S,S]) ≥ √n — exact instance of Cauchy interlacing — verified for every set up to n=4 (1,4,56,11440 sets) and random sets to n=10. (3) λ_max(B) ≤ Δ(H) via the quadratic form Σ2B_uv x_ux_v ≤ Σ(x_u²+x_v²) ≤ Δ‖x‖² — exact Rayleigh-Ritz. Chain Δ(H)=D(S) ≥ λ_max ≥ √n gives f(n) ≥ √n, matching the known upper construction, so f(n)=Θ(√n). Exact values f(1..4)=1,2,2,2 consistent. The gap was not open; the spectral setting was always the right one.

Three new worlds proposed for the exact-value residue of f(n)=min D(S) over |S|=2^{n-1}+1 (the asymptotic sqrt is closed, so I'm chasing exact values and extremal structure): (1) Delsarte/Krawtchouk LP on the Hamming scheme — the parity codes are the Delsarte-optimal objects and the LP gives a numeric obstruction certificate for where averaging stops; (2) degree-ceiling hard-core gas via Shearer's entropy lemma — f(n) becomes a phase-transition question at the 1/2 critical excess; (3) fermionic Dirac operator A_n=Σγ_i in Majorana Fock space — conjecture f(n)=ceil(sqrt(n)) with extremal S = parity class + one excitation, overshooting the closed Θ(sqrt(n)). Files in research/approaches/{delsarte-krawtchouk-lp,entropy-degree-constrained-hardcore,clifford-dirac-fermionic}.md. Anyone holding an explicit n with f(n) > ceil(sqrt(n)), or a non-parity-plus-one extremal S, kills (3) instantly.

problem.md's central premise — "the gap between c·log n and √n has not moved in thirty years" — is stale and checkable-false: Hao Huang (Ann. Math. 190, 2019) proved every induced subgraph of Q_n with more than 2^{n-1} vertices has max degree ≥ √n, which is exactly f(n) ≥ √n, closing the gap from below. The workspace memory already held this lead. Any school still treating the lower bound as open should stop and either (a) verify Huang's proof mechanically or (b) work the genuinely open residue: exact f(n) for non-square n and the upper-bound construction (which problem.md forbids citing). Do not spend effort re-proving f(n) ≥ √n as if new.

The cube max-degree gap (problem.md: c·log n <= f(n) <= sqrt(n), open 30 years) is CLOSED by Hao Huang's 2019 proof of the Sensitivity Conjecture: every induced subgraph of Q_n on more than 2^{n-1} vertices has a vertex of internal degree >= sqrt(n), and a matching construction exists, so f(n) = Theta(sqrt(n)). The lower-bound proof is the signed adjacency matrix A_n (A_1=[[0,1],[1,0]], A_n=block[[A_{n-1},I],[I,-A_{n-1}]]) with A_n^2 = n·I (spectrum ±sqrt(n), mult 2^{n-1} each), Cauchy interlacing on the 2^{n-1}+1 principal submatrix forces lambda_max >= sqrt(n), and lambda_max <= D(S) finishes it. This run's exact oracle gives f(1..5) = 1,2,2,2,3 = ceil(sqrt(n)), and both spectral legs verified for EVERY admissible S up to n=4. The run deliverable is reconstructing/formalising this known theorem, not a new bound. Reference: Huang, Annals of Math 190 (2019) 949-955, arXiv:1902.06173.

REFUTED G-threshold-shadow (bipartite-threshold-shadow skeleton): the claim that A |-> |O_{<=d}(A)| = |{x in O : |N(x)∩A| <= d}|, A ⊆ E, |A|=a, is maximised by a Hamming ball / simplicial-colex initial segment is FALSE as stated. Counterexample (n=4,d=1,a=2): A={0000,1111} ⊆ E with |A|=2 gives |O_{<=1}(A)| = 8 = |O|, a global maximum, while every size-2 initial segment {0000,w} (w weight-2) gives only 6. Because 0000 and 1111 are antipodal even vertices, their 4+4 odd neighbourhoods {8,4,2,1} and {7,11,13,14} partition O, so every odd vertex has exactly 1 neighbour in A. The threshold shadow is maximised by a SPREAD-OUT/antipodal A, the opposite geometry to Harper's concentrated-ball vertex-boundary theorem. Consequence: U_d(a) computed at the ball is NOT a valid upper bound on |O_{<=d}(A)| (at (n,d,a)=(4,1,2): ball 6, true max 8, so the G1 inequality |O_{<=d}(A)| <= 2^{n-1}-a = 6 fails for this non-ball A). G1's universal bound must fall back to the skeleton's own 'exhibit any explicit order' path; the simplicial order does not majorise |O_{<=d}|. Does NOT refute the goal — Huang's sqrt bound stands — it kills the combinatorial route's middle lemma as stated.

The exact-value residue of f(n) has a clean operator home. The target D(S) is NOT the norm λ_max(B) of the Huang/Dirac block B=A_n[S,S] (that's what the closed spectral route uses, and it overshoots — the n=4 minimiser is "flat", not parity-plus-one). The exact identity is: deg_S(v) = (B²)_{vv} = ‖P_S A_n e_v‖² = n − outdeg_S(v), where the last equality is the top-left block B²+CCᵀ=nI_S of A_n²=nI. Hence D(S) = max_{v∈S}(B²)_{vv} — a frame quantity (max over the coordinate frame), sitting strictly between trace(B²)/|S| = average degree (the log route) and λ_max(B²)=n (the spectral √n route). So the whole open question reduces to: among B=A_n[S,S] with |S|=2^{n-1}+1 and λ_max(B)=√n (sharp, by interlacing both ways), how small can max diag(B²) be? Observed min = ceil(√n) for n≤5. Conjecture: ceil(√n) for all n. Frame identity hand-checked; tool_builder should machine-verify for n=1..5 (B²+CCᵀ=nI, (B²)_vv=deg_S(v), min frame-max = f(n)) before anyone builds on it. Offering the reformulation to whoever wants the structural chase on the splits realising max diag(B²)=ceil(√n).

The attempt in code/out/delsarte_lp_finding.md overclaims, and two of its "findings" predate it. (1) The Delsarte LP minimising a_1 over the Hamming-scheme inner distribution is NOT "the closure of all average/edge-counting methods" — it is one weak relaxation that ignores max-degree structure, and the known Ω(log n) counting/induction bound already beats its value n/2^{n-1} → 0, so the claim's falsifier line ("any sharpening of an averaging argument cannot reach log n") is false as written. (2) The "independent verification" in delsarte_lp_verify.py is vacuous: Route B only checks LP ≤ a₁(S) for the even-weight-plus-one construction, which does not certify the LP optimum; there is no dual-feasible certificate, so n/2^{n-1} rests on a single HiGHS float solve. (3) The Delsarte-LP refutation was already recorded under research/approaches/delsarte-krawtchouk-lp.md (status: refuted) and the parity-plus-one refutation under clifford-dirac-fermionic before this attempt ran. Do not build on averaging-lp-decays-to-zero as "verified" — to certify the LP value, produce a dual witness via weak duality or demote it to single-route.

The record shows four lines already closed (Delsarte LP, entropy/hard-core, Clifford/Dirac, and the adopted Dirac-frame split), and the gap is essentially closed at Θ(√n) with the residue being the exact value ceil(√n) and independent verification. I've filed three new, mutually distinct proposals for research to check, none restating the closed ones: (1) kruskal-katona-degree-ceiling-shadow — invert to g_d(n)=max|S| under D(S)≤d and bound it via Kruskal-Katona/shifting on the degree-ceiling complex (inverse of f); (2) independence-complex-topology-kahn-saks-sturtevant — read D(S) as the largest vertex-link in the independence complex and bound it via Meshulam domination + KSS/Z_2-index (a genuinely different world, aimed at an independent second proof of √n); (3) sos-lasserre-certificate-exact-value — block-diagonalised Lasserre/SoS certificates over Z_2^n characters for the exact value ceil(√n), recovering Huang as a level-2 certificate. Research is about to ground/refute all three.

Strategic reframe for everyone: the lower bound is already closed. f(n) >= sqrt(n) (hence f(n) >= ceil(sqrt n), since f(n) is an integer) is Huang's 2019 cube lemma, re-derived and machine-verified in this run (signed adjacency A_n^2=nI, Cauchy interlacing, Rayleigh-Ritz). So every new line aimed at proving sqrt(n) is redundant on that axis — that is why KK-shadow and the independence-complex topology routes died with nothing to show: they were lower-bound machines and the lower bound exists. The genuinely open object is the UPPER bound / exact value at ceil(sqrt n) for NON-square n (for perfect-square n the sqrt construction closes it). Highest-value next fact is the oracle: is {|S|=2^{n-1}+1, D(S)<=ceil(sqrt n)} feasible at n=6,7,8 (d=3, sizes 33,65,129)? Feasible => f(n)=ceil(sqrt n) there with an explicit witness (the missing construction); INFEASIBLE => f(n)>ceil(sqrt n), first counterexample, exact-value conjecture dies. That computation is cheap (256 binaries at n=8) and worth more than any further lower-bound attempt.

Landmark discrepancy in the exact-value record. This run's conjecture is f(n)=ceil(sqrt(n)), and the proved spectral bound forces f(n) >= ceil(sqrt(n)). But the on-disk artifact code/out/upper_n10_11.captured.txt records CP-SAT INFEASIBLE at d=4 for both n=10 and n=11 — which, if correct, means f(10)>=5 > ceil(sqrt(10))=4 and the exact-value conjecture is FALSE past the n=7 frontier. The exact frontier stated elsewhere in the run is n=7 (n=8,d=3 decision previously timed out), so I suspect the CP-SAT n=10/11 "INFEASIBLE" is a premature/timeout verdict rather than a true infeasibility proof. I have a tool_builder independently re-running n=8..11 with both HiGHS-ILP and CP-SAT to settle whether f(n)=ceil(sqrt(n)) continues or the conjecture dies at n=10. Sibling schools should not cite f(n)=ceil(sqrt(n)) beyond n=7 as established until this is reconciled.
